article.title: Iowa lead bomb: Abby Martin says the real threat is ‘your army’
article.author: Zoe Alexandra
article.content: The Pentagon is set to explode five tons of lead azide next to a small town in Iowa on Wednesday. Abby Martin says that’s the real threat to the homeland: “It’s not Iran dropping a dirty bomb on us. It’s your army.” Middletown and communities across the interstate fallout radius are bracing for the toxic contamination of homes, the country’s corn supply, and the Mississippi River, after Trump passed the buck to Iowa’s incoming Democratic governor Rob Sand and a federal appeals court greenlit the blast. Martin, the Empire Files journalist and director of Earth’s Greatest Enemy, joins Rania Khalek and Zoe Alexandra to expose the US military’s devastating environmental footprint, from toxic waste and PFAS contamination at bases across the country to the pollution and destruction left behind by US wars abroad. Martin says the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant, an EPA Superfund site since 1990, is also “supplying arms to kill little girls in Gaza, in our name, with our tax dollars.” The tank shell that killed two ambulance paramedics attempting to rescue 6-year-old Hind Rajab was manufactured in Middletown. And the military industrial complex escapes accountability on the world stage, too: Martin slams the collapse of COP31 on Sunday – “What the hell are we doing? What are these conferences even about?” – and the exclusion of military emissions from climate reporting. Why does the world’s largest institutional polluter get a pass on the global climate debate? But Martin also points to a growing wave of grassroots resistance racking up wins. Communities across the US uniting in opposition to military bases and AI data centers are proof that militarism isn’t inevitable: “These are winnable fights.” Watch Abby Martin’s documentary Earth’s Greatest Enemy and learn more about her work with The Empire Files: https://empirefiles.tv/ Watch full episodes of BT Live, join breakthroughnews.org as a member today! #breakthroughnews ****** Rough transcript follows: [Interviewer:] Thank you so much for having me, you guys. It’s amazing to be here. [Speaker 2:] It’s so great to have you on, Abby. Let’s start with the Iowa story before we get into some of the other stuff. The army is saying that this stuff is too unstable to move, so instead, they’re going to blow it up in place as the safest option. How does five tons of degrading explosive, first of all, sit in bunkers for decades if it’s so unstable? And why is the solution always to dump the risk on the people next door? What’s happening here? [Abby Martin:] Yeah, I mean, first of all, this was an entirely avoidable crisis. Blowing up 10,000 pounds of lead explosives is a deliberate choice. They could have chemically neutralized this stuff, the entire stockpile, without a single explosion months ago. According to internal documents from the New York Times, this was a deliberate choice to opt for the explosion. There’s no accountability or answer to why that was. They’re opting to unleash lead-laden explosives, a toxic plume over 120 miles of cornfield. Iowa is the largest corn-producing state in America. This corn is in most processed foods, most animal feed. It just shows how this institution does not care about the law or people’s lives. They didn’t even notify people until five days before the initial planned detonation, including Iowa officials. This is the Pentagon’s playbook wherever it operates. Every place it stores toxic or hazardous materials, it cannot be trusted. We’re talking about everywhere around the world. It defers maintenance for these aging stockpiles like in Red Hill, Hawaii. They wait for something catastrophic to happen. In Iowa, these barrels were sitting there for 20 years. Suddenly, overnight, they’re too dangerous to move. So, what do they do? I guess we just have to blow them up. They do not actually incorporate the costs to the environment or human health. For them, this is the most cost-effective thing. But again, it’s an emergency of their own making because of their own negligence and disregard. I just can’t wrap my mind around the fact that an industry with a budget of over a trillion dollars cannot incorporate a safe disposal mechanism for these toxic chemicals that it is constantly manufacturing. They just know that they can override local governments and do this kind of stuff anyway. [Interviewer:] Really sinister stuff there. This plant has been a Superfund site since 1990. Explosives turned up in local streams and groundwater, and the army had to hook nearby homes up to rural water. In your film “Earth’s Greatest Enemy,” you document this exact scenario and pattern. How typical is Middletown and what they’re facing today? [Abby Martin:] Shockingly, most Superfund sites in the US are either current military installations or have previously housed military use. This is completely routine practice for the world’s largest polluter. Twenty-five years ago, the US government called to halt the destructive and deadly practice of open burning and open detonation. The military, as it often does, just completely ignored this and continues to use open burning and open detonation as the routine practice to dispose of toxic and hazardous materials. Dozens of military sites around the country are openly burning and detonating hazardous waste and material. One of the most disturbing things about making the documentary was that everywhere you went that the military operates, you find the same exact story. Everywhere around the world that the US has a base, you find the same toxic legacy of environmental destruction. We’re talking about nuclear radiation, Agent Orange, and chemical testing. But it’s not just the legacy of all the testing up until now. Guam, for example, we went to Tarague Beach where the Air Force is detonating and open burning on ancient ancestral land that is a sea turtle habitat that the Chamorro people have used for generations. They’re doing it just willy-nilly. For years and years, they’ve had to be sued by the local EPA. This is where it gets really tricky because the EPA authorizes this stuff. The very organization that is tasked with protecting the environment is actually giving the army emergency measures and provisions to do these horrific planet-destroying activities on a regular basis. You look at PFAS contamination, this is the next looming health disaster around the country. Every single military base has PFAS contamination seeping out into the groundwater. When there could have been safe disposal, safe alternatives decades ago, they choose to do this. We know the toxic legacy in Iraq and Afghanistan. We know the ecocide being committed now. These are just munitions. This is the lead and toxic compounds from just munitions that are exploded in wartime. But it’s so important to know that this is happening in relative peacetime to maintain a global military arsenal. It requires an insane amount of chemicals to treat the equipment, to maintain the engine parts to be mission-ready. It’s incomprehensible the amount of pollution this is causing. I just want to give you one statistic. The DoD reports through its toxic inventory release that it dumps 28 million pounds of toxic waste into the environment annually in the US. This number does not include tons of unreported chemicals and it does not include overseas bases. So just imagine how much this is happening, how much we can’t quantify. Again, it’s all happening completely extra-legally by the same government agencies that are supposed to be protecting our land and our health. [Interviewer:] Just to follow up on that, Abby, another area you follow closely is what’s happening in Gaza. The Nation actually traced shell fragments from the ambulance where two Palestinian paramedics were killed while trying to rescue Hen Rajab back to the same plant in Iowa. Talk about that connection. [Abby Martin:] I don’t even want to really talk about the imperial boomerang because it makes it seem like these weapons weren’t tested here on Black and brown populations before they were exported to indigenous communities and in these sacrifice zones all around the world. But it is such a visceral example of how everyone’s connected. We are all victims of this military machine. The very plant that is about to drop a dirty bomb on American citizens and poison our corn and our food supply and the Mississippi River is the same plant that is supplying arms to kill little girls in Gaza in our name with our tax dollars. It is just such an extreme example of how the military-industrial complex hits here and abroad and how it does not care. We are all expendable in the eyes of this beast. [Interviewer:] It’s so crazy, that connection. I wanted to ask you about COP 31, which just collapsed after record overtime with no deal and not even the words fossil fuels in the draft. The US didn’t even send an official delegation this time. Military emissions are still voluntary to report, and the US has stopped reporting them altogether. Can these summits ever mean anything while the biggest polluter isn’t even on the table? Even when the US does take a seat at the table, they never discuss the US military as your film “Earth’s Greatest Enemy” points out. [Abby Martin:] This COP has really revealed the futility of these things. I think we need to wrap it up, guys. Let’s wrap up these global conferences and get serious because it’s just a waste of money. It’s for the ruling class to go and pat themselves on the back and rehabilitate their greenwashing efforts and the clean energy initiatives that they’re doing to maintain neoliberalism and global capitalism. It’s such a slap in the face. Some countries in the global south were saying, “We are held hostage by an oil mafia that is running the climate agenda.” It’s always been essentially a farce because you’ve had people like Al Gore leading the effort with carbon capture, which is really cartoonish. Are we really capturing carbon cumulatively? It does nothing. It’s just a way for them to continue to extract fossil fuel and prevent what we actually need to do, which is stop drilling, keep the oil in the ground. For the first time in 17 years, this was the first time that the climate conference ended without a deal. Trump stopped sending delegations altogether. They have completely pulled out of this entire conference. But you have the main oil producers like Russia, Saudi Arabia leading the opposition, and because every country has veto power, no one can come to a unanimous decision. For the second COP in a row, they have not only left out the transition away from fossil fuels off the table, they have failed to even mention the culprit of who is the main driver of the climate catastrophe, which is fossil fuels. It is just absolutely comical at this point. It’s always been a farce. You go back to the Kyoto treaty led by Bill Clinton, and the Pentagon paved the way to have military emissions be exempt. For the last 20-plus years, we have not even counted cumulative emissions. If we’re not actually counting emissions, and if you look at US-led emissions, it’s more than half the world’s nations combined. That’s not even counting the 5% NATO mandate that Trump just deployed. We’re not even counting emissions, right? And now we’re not even talking about fossil fuels. So what the hell are we doing? What are these conferences even about? This one didn’t even talk about reparations for the global south like they promised last COP, which they paved a bunch of the Amazon rainforest to just fly out delegates anyway. It’s disgusting and insulting that the world is burning down around us, and we don’t even have the courage to muster to utter who’s driving the damage and destruction. [Interviewer:] I highly recommend people who haven’t seen it really do check out your film because the confrontation you have questioning US officials about the emissions of the US military and it not being counted is incredible. They don’t have an answer because they are complicit in this. That COP was worthwhile for getting that on the record at the very least. [Abby Martin:] Yeah, incredible stuff there. Going back to the situation in Iowa, it’s a small town. Environmental groups and local officials temporarily pushed back. The detonation is scheduled for tomorrow, but they did force the army at one moment to back down three different times in the past week. What’s the lesson there for Middletown and anyone living next to a base? I think the lesson is community organization. Even though this looks like it will happen, we know that it will, despite community pushback. They put these plants where there’s a low density of human population, even though it will have widespread effects on human health and the contamination of our food. They’re still putting it in a town with a couple hundred people because they know there won’t be widespread community pushback or they can kind of operate extra-legally and override the local government there. What we’ve seen with the midterm sweep and especially with the data center moratoriums is how viscerally people are reacting against big tech and personifying the face of the military-industrial complex with these data centers. They are winning. It’s not just a repudiation of Trump. It’s a repudiation of this entire kind of war, the military-industrial complex, the war with Iran. People are synonymizing it like you said, the Hen Rajab connection. Gaza has been a catalyst in the connective tissue for people to really understand how this affects everyone, and they’re manifesting into these fights against data centers. We’ve seen the success stories all across the US. Data centers and the war with Iran were some of the main issues that people pointed to as why they came out and voted in the midterms. We’ve seen big broad coalitions building with those success stories being pushed back against the data centers. Whether it’s a base contaminating your water with forever chemicals or a data center trying to override the local community, these are winnable fights. Divesting your institutions from weapons contractors, defeating that inevitability of militarism and empire being a permanent state. Going back to COP where Nancy Pelosi said, “Yeah, well, you know, the military is the solution.” They’ve just basically hung their heads in shame and thrown their hands up and said the empire is the solution for the problems that it causes. We really have to push back against that kind of military mindset and figure out how we can reclaim our agency here and win. [Interviewer:] I want to broaden that out a bit, Abby, because we’re talking about the midterms. Democrats did win big because Trump’s agenda is just so unbelievably unpopular. But one thing that’s been so striking about this election cycle and the conversation in general is the way the issue of climate change has just dropped off as a topic. I can’t remember the last time I saw it even raised. I wanted to get your thoughts on that danger and that this really isn’t an issue that registers so much politically anymore, even as so many progressive ideas are becoming mainstream across the country. [Abby Martin:] I think it could be best articulated with just how immediate the measures are of relief for people in this country. You said it yourself in the previous segment. We’re talking about 60% or more of Americans who are literally surviving paycheck to paycheck. They have no savings in the bank if there’s an emergency. Bread on their table, gas in their tank, these things are so immediate. Yes, they can connect them to the war abroad. Yes, they can connect them to big tech and the control of the military-industrial complex, but it’s harder to resolve the immediate urgency of climate change. On top of that, it’s just kind of fallen to the periphery. What scares me is the fact that fewer Americans actually believe in man-made climate change now than they did five years ago. I honestly point to the culpability of the mainstream media, the corporate media that acts on behalf of these power brokers and oil companies. They are subsidized by the very same structures of power that we need to be holding to account for poisoning the planet. The big banks, the big oil companies. This is hugely problematic. You can see this displayed with Gaza. The fact that Americans don’t even know how many Palestinians versus Israelis have died. This is malpractice. This is a criminal component of the media that obfuscates the truth and the reality that should be displayed on our nightly news. The fact that the military is poisoning and killing us all. It’s not Iran dropping a dirty bomb on us. It’s your army. The one that we worship. The one that we praise at sporting events. This is the one that’s going to kill us and poison your family and your earth. I just point to the fact that Americans simply are not told, and the lack of political education is astounding when it should be on the nightly news. As the world continues to burn around us, as climate change becomes more visceral and immediate than ever, it should be incorporated into every single policy prescription. But I think we all know why it’s not. [Interviewer:] Well, on that note, Abby, we appreciate you so much. I want to once again encourage everybody. If you haven’t seen “Earth’s Greatest Enemy,” even if you think you know, you don’t know. It is such an eye-opening film and it speaks to basically everything we’ve talked about in a really important and impactful way. Go watch “Earth’s Greatest Enemy,” support Abby’s work. Abby, thank you so much for joining us. We appreciate you so much.
